newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa holds slim gains, switches active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa holds slim gains, switches active.

text.p: Cocoa futures held slim gains at the close on Wednesday. Traders said dealings centred on switch trades, with active Dec 1997/Dec 1998 switch changing hands at 81 stg.
The day's volume reached 6,283 lots, comprising some 800 lots in Dec/Dec switch and a further 400 in AA trades.
"It's mainly switch-bound. It's quite a lacklustre day and funds have stopped selling for now," said one floor trader.
September, London's benchmark, stood at 986 stg a tonne at the close, up 11 on the day after a 12-stg range with a high at 992.
Earlier, others said the gains followed short-covering buying and a technical rebound to a fund-led sell-off earlier in the week.
The rebound was quite encouraging despite sterling's renewed strength against the German mark, they said.
"It (the currency move) just effectively overshadowed the market," said one. "It probably detered the rally but the market did quite well despite sterling."
But analysts said the weak technical picture would not change until September regains a footing above 1,000 stg, seen as the immediate hurdle.

Sterling raced to top 3.0878 German mark, strongest since September 1989, on Wednesday morning before holding at 3.0780/90 in late trade in Europe. This compares with 3.0425/35 late Tuesday in Europe.
Fundamentally, traders were keeping a watchful eye on cocoa crop development in West Africa. A fuller picture on the size of the 1997/98 Ivorian crop is unlikely to emerge until next month, some say.
Among latest crop news, Ivory Coast's dry season in July favoured drying of mid-crop cocoa (May-Sept) but will not damage pod growth for 1997/98 (Oct-April), analysts said.
Elsewhere, Ivory Coast is likely to raise its reference cocoa and coffee farmgate prices in the 1997/98 (Oct-Sept) season, buyers and exporters say.
"My feeling is that we will have a rise for both cocoa and coffee," said one industry buyer. "There are a number of elements pointing to an increase, but none to a decrease."
Donors in 1996/97 have pushed for increases as part of talks on disbursement of outstanding amounts of a $150 million agricultural
Ivory Coast set a cocoa farmgate price of 315 CFA a kilo for 1996/97, unchanged from the 1995/96 year, although export duties were cut.
